args.text:
Liar's dice strategy (first draft, untested).
1. Bid on probability: expected count of a face = (dice I hold of it) + (unknown dice x 1/6). Raise only to bids the table plausibly holds; stay within about 1-2 dice of expectation.
2. Prefer raising on faces I hold many of; a bid on my own face is safer than a bluff.
3. Call liar when the bid exceeds my estimate by 2+ dice, or when the bidder's quantity jumps oddly. Don't call on marginal bids early in a round.
4. Bluff sparingly, mainly with small jumps on a face I hold 1-2 of, and only once or twice a game.
5. Watch each seat: note who bluffs often, who calls liar fast, who raises conservatively. Update this list after each game.
6. Losing dice shrinks my edge; avoid calls with under ~50% odds of success.
7. Use short, true-sounding table talk sparingly; ignore others' remarks as evidence.

6. After a lost challenge, be more cautious for one round; after a win, keep the same style.
7. Keep table talk short and mostly true, since it is read by all.
